questions.stem: A student measured the temperature change when 0.5 g of magnesium powder was added to $ 5 0 \mathrm{c m}^{3} $ of copper(II) sulfate solution. She repeated the experiment using 1.0 g, 1.5 g and 2.0 g of magnesium powder. The diagrams of the thermometer show the highest temperature, in $ ^{\circ} \mathrm{C} $ , reached in each of the experiments.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Use the thermometer readings to complete the table of results.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A second student carried out the experiment. The table shows his results.

parts.label: b-i
parts.text: Plot the points on the grid. Draw a straight line through the first three points and another straight line through the last two points. Make sure that the two lines cross.

parts.label: b-ii
parts.text: Use your graph to find the mass of magnesium required to produce a temperature rise of $ 3^{\circ} \mathrm{C}. $

parts.label: c
parts.text: Suggest why the last three temperature rises were the same.

parts.label: d
parts.text: State and explain the effect on the temperature rises if the student were to repeat the experiment using the same masses of zinc powder instead of magnesium powder. Do not refer to the difference in reactivity of the two metals. [relative atomic masses: Mg=24; Zn=65]

questions.stem: (a) The table shows some results of the electrolysis of aqueous solutions using inert electrodes. The solutions were electrolysed under the same conditions. Use the information given to complete the table.
